searchText: ah yes -- they could go either way as long as there is some schema to simplify processing i had originally leaned toward "front of block" but after thinking some more feel that "back of block" is more natural and i missed an edit. thanks for pointing it out, i'll go update now! yes, we will have to extend all of the existing infra to support this "operation" class of object if we go the 4895 route this EIP is a bit light on what it could contain as i mainly wanted to sketch out the idea and then circulate it to get feedback 4895 is "cleaner" but requires invasive changes 4863 mixes concerns a bit but only requires supporting a new 2718-style transaction type which is a much smaller ask i expect to get broader feedback from client implementers on the next ACD (this friday) and if we get serious about 4895 then i can consider fleshing out more of that EIP if you want to dig into some of the convo already, go check out the <#745077610685661265> channel starting from my (duplicate) post on march 11

excerpts.author: ralexstokes
excerpts.content:
ah yes -- they could go either way as long as there is some schema to simplify processing 

i had originally leaned toward "front of block" but after thinking some more feel that "back of block" is more natural

and i missed an edit. thanks for pointing it out, i'll go update now!

excerpts.author: ralexstokes
excerpts.content:
yes, we will have to extend all of the existing infra to support this "operation" class of object if we go the 4895 route

this EIP is a bit light on what it could contain as i mainly wanted to sketch out the idea and then circulate it to get feedback

4895 is "cleaner" but requires invasive changes

4863 mixes concerns a bit but only requires supporting a new 2718-style transaction type which is a much smaller ask

i expect to get broader feedback from client implementers on the next ACD (this friday) and if we get serious about 4895 then i can consider fleshing out more of that EIP
